clue.text: Glower in sack race

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them from a job
to race is to fly, to move at great speed

explanation.surface: Someone scowls while taking part in a sack race at a school sports day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glower' looks like a scowl, but read it as glow-er, something that glows. Rufus T. Firefly is also Groucho Marx's character in Duck Soup, one of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A firefly is an insect whose body gives off light, so it is literally one that glows.

clue.text: One thrice involved in being more scratchworthy

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone muses that tripling a number makes it more of an irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles I (One) with THRICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something itchier makes you want to scratch it more, a playful coinage for that comparative.

clue.text: Praise for report of old tax

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words that follow are to be said aloud

parts.note: an ex-toll, a toll no longer charged, is an old tax

explanation.surface: Someone is commended for writing an account of a historic levy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report of' signals that EX-TOLL is spoken, giving the verb for praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Uncultivated to blow off with loud noise

indicators.note: off means awry or wrong, so these letters go out of their usual order

parts.note: a row is a din or racket

explanation.surface: Someone boorish might go off with a bang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' gives LOWB, a scramble; 'to' is only a link joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowbrow means lacking in culture or refinement, so uncultivated in taste.

clue.text: Old Nick confines women to void

indicators.note: to confine is to hold inside, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: to negate is to nullify or void

explanation.surface: The Devil locks up women to banish them to emptiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Nick' looks like the Devil, but nick is British slang for prison: NEWGATE was London's notorious old jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Newgate was a historic London prison, and a nick is a slang word for a jail.

clue.text: Attempts to be heard as South African

indicators.note: something heard is spoken, so the letters are pronounced aloud

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa or South African; said as plural letters, S-As

explanation.surface: Someone tries to sound like they come from South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, SAs, letter by letter, gives 'ess-ays'.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is an attempt or trial, as in essaying a difficult task.

clue.text: Runner has honey laced with drug

indicators.note: laced means mixed in or tangled, so the letters are blended together

explanation.surface: An athlete is found with honey that has been spiked with narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laced' mixes HONEY and DRUG together; 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A greyhound is a racing dog, a runner on the track.

clue.text: See 27
One of a pair of crowns?

definitions.text: One of a pair of crowns?

parts.words: One of a pair of crowns?
parts.note: a crown is a ruler, so one of two joint monarchs is half a ruler; it is also a gold coin worth two silver crowns

explanation.walkthrough: A crown was an old British coin worth five shillings; two of them made ten shillings, the value of the coin wanted. The question mark flags the joint-monarch reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The coin was worth ten shillings, two crowns, and a co-ruler is half a monarch.

clue.text: Shoo shoo shoo-sha-boogy

definitions.meaning: an order to go away at once
nonsense syllables of the kind jazz singers improvise

explanation.walkthrough: SCAT means clear off, and it is also wordless improvised jazz singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Scat is both an exclamation shooing someone off and the jazz style of nonsense vocals.

clue.text: We harvest nothing organic at all

indicators.note: organic suggests something that grows and changes form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: nothing is O, the zero shape

explanation.surface: Farmers complain they reap nothing from their organic crops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organic' looks like describing the farm produce, but it rearranges WEHARVEST with O.
explanation.definitionFit: Whatsoever is an intensifier meaning at all, as in no doubt whatsoever.

clue.text: One preparing meal for runner crossing line

indicators.note: crossing is taken as straddling, so one piece goes across the other

parts.note: a miler is an athlete who runs the mile

explanation.surface: A cook makes food for an athlete who is about to cross the finish line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts L inside MILER. Gordon Miller is Groucho's character in Room Service.
explanation.definitionFit: A miller grinds grain into meal or flour.

clue.text: Welsh fervour about to be conveyed by aptitude for moving part

indicators.note: conveyed means carried, so one piece is carried within another

parts.note: a feel for something is an aptitude for it

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: hwyl is a Welsh word for passionate fervour, especially in song or oratory

explanation.surface: Passionate Welsh feeling is transmitted by a gift for something that moves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives LYWH and 'to be conveyed by' sets it inside. Wolf J. Flywheel is Groucho's character in The Big Store.
explanation.definitionFit: A flywheel is a heavy rotating wheel in a machine, one of its moving parts.

clue.text: Dead perch (if 2's involved) might be washed up

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for dead, as for died in records

indicators.note: involved means wrapped up in, so these letters go inside

parts.note: perch and rod are both old measures of length
2 is the number two, with 's just meaning is

explanation.surface: A dead fish might wash ashore, perhaps with a second one included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' sets the pair inside. 'Perch' looks like a fish but is the old length measure. Otis B. Driftwood is Groucho's character in A Night at the Opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Driftwood is wood that floats about at sea and gets washed up on beaches.

clue.text: Can't go wrong when pudding has some alcohol content

parts.note: a fool is a cold fruit and cream dessert
proof is the measure of how much alcohol a spirit contains

explanation.surface: Nothing can spoil a dessert once it has been laced with booze.
explanation.walkthrough: A FOOL is a British pudding of puréed fruit folded into cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Something foolproof is so simple it cannot go wrong, however it is used.

clue.text: Property of match that's heading to conclusion

indicators.note: the head letter goes to the end, like moving to the conclusion

parts.note: to match is to equal

explanation.surface: Something about a football fixture that is reaching its finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading to conclusion' moves the first E of EQUAL to the end. S. Quentin Quale is Groucho's character in Go West.
explanation.definitionFit: In philosophy a quale is a quality or property as experienced, such as redness.

clue.text: Experimental biology sheds by arctic quarters

indicators.note: experimental means trial and change, so the letters are rearranged
sheds means casts off, so some letters are taken away from the pool

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lab tries out work on biology in huts beside polar living quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: BIOLOGY loses the B and Y of BY, and 'Experimental' rearranges the leftover IOLOG.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a snow-block dwelling of the Arctic, a place to live there.

clue.text: Crab and duck featured as 1, 12, 13, 14, 16, 23 and 24

parts.note: a crab is a grumpy person, a grouch
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A crustacean and a waterbird appear among a list of numbered items.
explanation.walkthrough: Groucho Marx played Firefly, Miller, Flywheel, Driftwood, Quale, Loophole and Hammer in Marx Brothers films.
explanation.definitionFit: Groucho Marx played all those named characters across the Marx Brothers films.

clue.text: Actor's hung-over? That is universal

definitions.note: the 's is short for is, joining the actor to his description

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: draped means hung, as cloth is
U is the film certificate for universal

explanation.surface: A performer admits to a hangover, and claims everyone has one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses DRAPED, giving DEPARD; 'hung-over' reads as a hangover. Gérard Depardieu is the French actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Gérard Depardieu is a famous French film actor.

clue.text: Inability to communicate with a local on the continent

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the first pieces sit over the last

parts.note: a local is a pub, and PH stands for public house
Asia is the largest continent

explanation.surface: Struggling to talk with the regulars at a pub abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain one's 'local' is the neighbourhood pub, PH (public house) on maps.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphasia is a disorder, often from brain injury, that impairs speech and language.

clue.text: Carrying on outside with stolen kiss

indicators.note: with something stolen means it is taken away, so letters are removed

parts.note: external means outside
X stands for a kiss, as at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone steals a kiss outdoors and keeps on going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with stolen' takes X out of EXTERNAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means going on for ever, continuing without end.

clue.text: Almost lose sight of bogey

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to go blind is to lose one's sight

explanation.surface: A golfer nearly misses seeing the ball dropped for a bogey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the D of GO BLIND. 'bogey' looks like golf, but it is a bogeyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A bogey is an evil spirit or bogeyman, as is a goblin.

clue.text: Stakes returned by sounding out all means to avoid law

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: a pool is the total of stakes in a bet

indicators.note: sounding out means pronouncing, so the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: whole means all

explanation.surface: A gambler's winnings are returned after spreading word of a way round the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' gives a backward run of four letters. J. Cheever Loophole is Groucho's character in At the Circus.
explanation.definitionFit: A loophole is a gap in a law or contract that lets one evade it.

clue.text: A very short way to split the woman's pound

indicators.note: to split means to divide open, so these letters go inside

parts.note: her is the possessive of she
mm, millimetre, is a tiny distance

explanation.surface: A tiny path divides a woman's money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to split' sets the middle letters inside. 'pound' looks like money but means hit. Mr Hammer is Groucho's character in The Cocoanuts.
explanation.definitionFit: To hammer is to pound, to strike repeatedly and hard.

clue.text: Worth some ritual passage

indicators.note: a passage is a stretch of text, so the answer runs through these words

explanation.surface: A rite of passage is said to have value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passage' signals the run inside 'some ritual'; the surface plays on rite of passage.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit means worth or excellence, a synonym.

clue.text: 5-11 and 11-18 makes loss each go

definitions.note: these are ranges of years for pupils, primary and secondary in Britain

indicators.note: makes means forms or creates, so the letters are formed into something new

explanation.surface: A sports result: a defeat is chalked up for each attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges LOSS, EACH and GO. In Britain children go to primary school from 5 to 11 and secondary from 11 to 18.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages five to eleven and eleven to eighteen cover the years of compulsory schooling in Britain.

clue.text: Where and by what one may be saved to be successful

definitions.text: Where and by what one may be saved
definitions.meaning: a boxer is saved in the arena by the gong ending the round
to hit the mark, from a fairground strength test

explanation.walkthrough: A boxer can be saved by the bell inside the ring. At a fairground 'high striker' a mallet blow that rings the bell at the top wins.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringing the bell is an idiom for succeeding, as at a fairground strength test.

clue.text: Limit prisoner's punishment

parts.note: con, a convict, is a prisoner; the 's is just a link
a fine is a penalty or punishment

explanation.surface: A ceiling is set on the penalty given to inmates.
explanation.definitionFit: To confine is to limit or restrict within bounds.

clue.text: Some roofing provided by worker in some foundation

indicators.note: in means inside, so the worker sits inside the other piece

parts.note: a pile is a post driven in as a foundation
an ant is a worker in crosswords, from worker ants

explanation.surface: Roofers are supplied by a labourer working on the building's base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some roofing' looks like part of the wordplay but is the definition; a pile is a post sunk to support a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantile is a curved roof tile, so pantiles make up some roofing.
